evidence.fact: Replication lagged until required WAL segments had already been removed, and WAL archiving was not enabled, forcing manual re-synchronization.
The surviving staging snapshot took about 18 hours to copy and restored the database only to an earlier point in time.
The normal pg_dump path had silently failed because a PostgreSQL 9.2 client targeted PostgreSQL 9.6, alert email was rejected, and nobody regularly tested restoration.
Registered remediations included backup monitoring, point-in-time recovery, continuous archiving, automated restore testing, and explicit durability ownership.

observedFailure: A nominal backup process existed but produced no usable artifact, its failure alert was lost, replication recovery destroyed the remaining copy, and no routine restore test exposed the gap.
